One note before the plan: this workspace isn't a git repo and has no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or check open items. I didn't change any files, so nothing needs pushing. I ran film-crew as a short pass and kept everything in this reply; I didn't write the 00–10 files or run the validator.

**Assumptions (no questions asked):**
- **Concept:** "From the first word to the final frame." A script is written, turns into a production, then into a wall of finished episodes, and ends on the red triangle.
- **One Seedance call of 30 s** with 6 hard cuts. One call keeps the grade and light the same across all shots.
- **No text, numbers or logo inside the generation.** The brand guide says never to retype or redraw the signature, and AI text comes out unreliable. The text and the real logo PNG go on as overlays in CapCut.
- **Red appears in at most one small element per shot.** Shots 1 and 4 have none.
- **Sound is effects only:** no music, no voice, no subtitles. You add a licensed track in the edit.
- **Shot length:** 30 s ÷ ~5 s per shot = 6 shots.
- **The actor in shot 4** is a fictional woman in her thirties, not a real person.

## Shot plan

| # | Time | Shot | Red element | How it cuts to the next shot | Overlay (in edit) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0–5 s | Extreme close-up: a fountain pen nib writes on white paper, then lifts. Slow push-in. | none | Ends on blank white paper; shot 2 starts top-down on the same white page. | — |
| 2 | 5–10 s | Camera rises from the page to show a stack and rows of bound scripts on a graphite desk. | ribbon bookmark | Hard cut on the clapper sound. | SCREENWRITING |
| 3 | 10–15 s | Dark film set: a blank clapperboard snaps shut; behind it a cinema camera and crew silhouettes in haze. | camera tally light | Size jump from medium shot to close-up, key light stays frame-left. | FULL PRODUCTION |
| 4 | 15–20 s | Close-up of an actress, side-lit; she lifts her eyes to the lens and holds. | none | Match cut: her same close-up now appears on a monitor. | — |
| 5 | 20–25 s | Dolly back from that monitor to a wall of dozens of black-and-white episode screens. | record dot on one screen | Hard cut to black on a low boom. | 48 PROJECTS · 2,300+ EPISODES (2,300+ in red) |
| 6 | 25–30 s | Pure black; a red triangle fades in at centre and holds still from 27 s to 30 s. | the triangle | End card. | `maghakian_logo_light.png`, placed so its triangle covers the generated one |

**9:16 layout:** keep the subject in the middle third, and keep the bottom 20% and top 10% clear for the Reels interface.

**Overlay type:** small uppercase sans with wide letter-spacing, in white. Red is used for one word only (2,300+).

**Risks:**
- **Six shots in one call may blur together.** If a shot fails, regenerate just that one as a 5 s Omni clip: paste its slice plus the "Global settings" block.
- **Stray text may appear** on the clapper or the paper. The prompt bans readable text; if it still shows up, regenerate that shot.
- **Shot 6 triangle:** the logo's triangle has to line up with the generated one. If it doesn't fit cleanly, put the logo over plain black instead.

## FINAL

**Settings (Dreamina, Seedance 2.5):**
- Mode: Omni Reference (timeline-30)
- Duration: 30 s
- Ratio: 9:16
- Resolution: 720p (use 1080p if your UI offers it)
- Uploads: none
- Output: native sound effects on; add music, text overlays and the logo PNG (`.claude/skills/director-desk/assets/maghakian_logo_light.png`) in the edit

**Prompt:**
```text
30-second cinematic brand teaser in six shots joined by hard cuts: a screenplay is handwritten, becomes a film production, becomes a wall of finished episodes, and ends on a single small red triangle in darkness. Vertical composition.

[Global settings]
Environment and texture: a quiet film studio at night; extreme real physical texture — paper fibre, wet ink sheen, matte black metal, dust floating in light beams, fine film grain.
Visual style: cinematic realism, near-monochrome grade — deep pure blacks, graphite-grey midtones, clean white highlights. No colour anywhere except one small deep crimson red element (#D90429) in the shots where it is named. One hard key light from frame left, deep shadows, shallow depth of field.
Camera language: vertical framing, subject kept in the centre third of the frame, nothing important in the bottom fifth or top tenth; slow, precise, motivated moves only; every shot ends with the camera still.
Performance core: calm, confident, crafted; precision over spectacle.
Prohibited: subtitles, captions, on-screen text, readable words, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks; background music; voices or speech; any colour other than black, white, grey and the single named red element; red backgrounds or large red areas; more than one red element per shot; whip pans, shaky handheld, lens flares, glitch effects, light leaks.

[Storyboard]
[0-5s] Shot 1 — The first word
Physical directives: extreme close-up from a three-quarter top angle. A black fountain pen nib writes one line of illegible handwriting in black ink on bright white paper; the wet ink line glistens. At 4s the pen lifts out of frame upward and the frame holds on the white paper and the fresh ink. Slow push-in throughout. No red in this shot.
Sound: nib scratching on paper, soft paper rustle, quiet room tone.
Intent: everything begins on the page.

[5-10s] Shot 2 — The library of scripts
Physical directives: hard cut. Starts top-down on a white handwritten page filling the frame; the camera rises straight up, revealing it is the top page of a tall stack of bound screenplays on a graphite-grey desk, surrounded by dozens of bound scripts in neat rows. One script has a thin deep crimson red ribbon bookmark hanging out — the only colour in the frame. Ends on a still wide top-down view.
Sound: soft page riffle, paper settling, room tone.
Intent: volume and craft — years of writing.

[10-15s] Shot 3 — Production
Physical directives: hard cut. Medium shot on a dark film set in light haze. A plain black clapperboard with no writing on it is held at the centre of frame and snaps shut at 11s, then lowers out of frame bottom. Behind it, softly out of focus, a cinema camera on a dolly with one small red tally light lit, crew silhouettes, one hard light beam from frame left. Ends still.
Sound: sharp clapper snap at 11s, then a hushed set, faint dolly wheel creak.
Intent: the script becomes a production.

[15-20s] Shot 4 — The performance
Physical directives: hard cut. Close-up of an actress in her thirties, dark hair pulled back, black turtleneck, lit hard from frame left with half her face in shadow, real skin texture with fine pores. She starts looking down, slowly lifts her eyes to the lens by 17s, takes one slow breath and holds a steady, focused gaze until 20s. Locked camera with a very slow push-in. No red in this shot.
Sound: her soft breath, quiet room tone.
Intent: the human truth at the centre of every story.

[20-25s] Shot 5 — The episodes
Physical directives: hard cut. Starts on the same close-up of the same actress, now seen on a monitor screen. The camera dollies straight back, revealing a dark edit suite and a wall of dozens of monitors in a tight grid, each showing a different black-and-white scene: faces, streets, rooms. One small red recording dot glows on a single monitor. Ends with the monitor wall filling the frame, camera still.
Sound: low electronic hum, faint keyboard clicks.
Intent: hundreds of finished episodes.

[25-30s] Shot 6 — The mark
Physical directives: hard cut to pure black. A small deep crimson red triangle (#D90429), point up, fades in at the exact centre of the frame with a faint soft glow and rests perfectly still on pure black from 27s to 30s. Nothing else in the frame.
Sound: one deep low cinematic boom at 25s, decaying into silence.
Intent: the signature of the studio.

[Global supplement]
Keep the near-monochrome grade, the hard key light from frame left and the fine film grain identical in all six shots. Hard cuts only, no dissolves. Pure video: no subtitles, no on-screen text, no logos, no background music, no voices. Only one small red element per shot, as named; none in shots 1 and 4.
```
